Phoropter-tui is a terminal reader of phoropter's pages, built over two days in its own repository. It's been a second reader of the profile, and it found the gaps selvage and osier closed. It plans its own work in this format. Six of its plans have landed, among them ramie (reading the draft), batiste (answering from the TUI), and nankeen (landed plans aren't edited from the TUI). Every time one of its plans needed a reason from phoropter, it could only cite it in prose: "loden says", "sorrel declined". Every time phoropter needed something from it, the request went through a brief, for-phoropter.md, carried between repositories by hand. Both are what two repositories cost. In one repository they're anchors and drafts.

Other people's readers still build against the public API, the served pages, and send pull requests. This one is first-party, the way a CLI lives with the service it reads.

Decision: The TUI comes in with its history, under tui/, and its plans join plans/

where CLAUDE.md file page

quote Jeff may build a TUI on them, in another

Because (Jeff): "declines, etc. here should point at things from that repo." In phoropter-tui, one commit moves everything under tui/ except plans/. Then this repository merges it with git merge --allow-unrelated-histories. Commits keep their SHAs, so every base: and head: in the TUI's plans still names a commit here. The plan names don't collide with phoropter's. CLAUDE.md's "in another repo" changes to tui/.

Decision: Plans from both sides can point at each other

where plans/2026-10-30-gimlet.md › Cross-repo anchors are shown as text

entry Decision: Cross-repo anchors are shown as text in gimlet

Because (Claude, not asked): gimlet showed cross-repo anchors as text, since v0 reads one repository. That stays true. The TUI coming in is what makes its references resolve. A TUI plan can anchor a phoropter entry and revisits: one, and phoropter's pages list TUI entries under "anchored by". The next TUI draft is the first case: it revisits loden (the one draft, at the root). Jeff found more evidence while this was a draft: the TUI, run from phoropter-tui, couldn't answer it, because it looked for the draft in its own repository.

Decision: The brief becomes drafts and shelf seeds

where plans/2026-10-30-gimlet.md › A separate brief beside the plan

entry Decline: A separate brief beside the plan in gimlet

Because (Jeff, then Claude): gimlet declined a separate brief because "two copies of what to build can disagree." for-phoropter.md is one. Its open items become seeds in shelf/, each restated into a draft when it's picked up:

  • › paths resolving (new-never-resolved, where-path-unresolved, view-no-code)
  • file pages (ranges, symbol anchors on their file, a place lookup, the blob id)
  • what's already at a draft's places, whose condition is met
  • reasons to re-check, and Holds while:
  • a Select's chosen options as properties
  • where indexing lives, with a plugin for each language

The brief stays in tui/docs/ as the record of what the second reader found, marked as superseded by shelf/.

Decision: The TUI reads only what phoropter serves, and the rule says why

where CLAUDE.md file page

quote **The rels and microdata are a public API.**

Because (Jeff and Claude): the TUI found the profile's gaps because it could read nothing else, and its gaps ledger only works while that's true. tui/CLAUDE.md says the TUI is tested only against served or built pages. It never reads src/, and never imports or shells out to phoropter's code beyond running its dev server. Go and TypeScript can't import each other by accident, which helps. When the ledger goes quiet, it should be because phoropter closed a gap, never because the TUI started reading past the pages.

Decision: Two CLAUDE.md files, the root one pointing at the TUI's

where CLAUDE.md file page

quote **Claude commits; Jeff pushes.**

Because (Claude, not asked): a session in tui/ needs the TUI's rules (the boundary, the ledger, the Go dependency pins). A session at the root needs to know the TUI is a reader whose gaps are phoropter's to close. The root file gets one line saying so and pointing at tui/CLAUDE.md. The TUI's file drops its "never edit ../phoropter" rule, since it's here now. Its boundary is the public API, not the directory.

Decision: Each side keeps its own tests

where package.json file page

quote "test": "node --test test/"

Because (Claude, not asked): someone sending phoropter a pull request shouldn't need Go installed. npm test stays phoropter's, and go test ./... in tui/ stays the TUI's. The TUI's fixtures are sites built by phoropter, and when the profile changes they're rebuilt in the same work, which is what being one repository is for. npm test doesn't run the TUI's tests even when Go is installed: two commands, each side's own, and a change to the profile names both in its plan (Jeff).

Decision: The lineage copies come to the root

where .gitignore file page

quote .loom/cart/

Because (Jeff): phoropter-tui keeps .loom/ committed (copies of the annotating and cart agreements this work descends from), with .loom/cart/ ignored. Phoropter already ignores .loom/cart/ and restates the same annotating agreement. The copies describe the whole repository's lineage, not the TUI's alone, so .loom/ moves to the root rather than under tui/. Nothing in either side references .loom paths, as both CLAUDE.md files say. The other choice was tui/.loom/ (Jeff).

Decision: phoropter-tui's own repository is archived, pointing here

where (new) tui/README.md file page

made by the work, so there is nothing to resolve

Because (Claude, not asked): two live copies can disagree, for the same reason as the brief. After the merge, the old repository's README says where the TUI lives now, and Jeff archives it on GitHub. Jeff pushes. Nothing here changes a remote.

Decline: Rewriting the TUI's plans for their new paths

Because (the guide): plans are read as written. The TUI's plans anchor internal/tui/screens.go and the like. At their base commits those paths are right, and they resolve. At the generated commit they've moved to tui/internal/… and show as no-file. That's true: the files moved. A later TUI plan anchors the new paths.

Decline: One language for both

Because (Claude, not asked): the TUI is a reader of the public API, and a reader in a different language than the server is the strongest proof the API is public. It's Go, with Bubble Tea, because that's what a terminal reader is good in. Rewriting it to share code would undo the reason it's worth having here.

Guess: The TUI stays an outside reader inside this repository

Answered in the as-built: not tested.

Disproved if: a change to the TUI reads src/, imports phoropter's modules, or closes a gap in the TUI's ledger without phoropter's pages changing.
